hwreck-01-c1.text: Jo Marchant (2016). Human Skeleton Found on Famed Antikythera Shipwreck. Scientific American (reprinted from Nature).
hwreck-01-c1.quote: Unless covered by sediment or otherwise protected, the bodies of shipwreck victims are usually swept away and decay, or are eaten by fish.
hwreck-01-c1.claim: Unless they are covered by sediment or protected in some other way, the bodies of shipwreck victims are normally swept away to decay or be eaten by fish.

hwreck-01-c2.text: CORDIS, European Commission (2019). Strategies for the protection of shipwrecks in the Baltic Sea against forthcoming attack by wood degrading marine borers (WRECKPROTECT): reporting. CORDIS.
hwreck-01-c2.quote: It is estimated that around 100 000 shipwrecks are present in the Baltic today and at least 6000 are of high archaeological importance.
hwreck-01-c2.claim: One estimate puts the number of wrecks in the Baltic at around 100,000, at least 6,000 of them of high archaeological importance.

hwreck-01-c3.text: Simon Clabby (2024). Time and its effect on the Mary Rose. Mary Rose Trust.
hwreck-01-c3.quote: The starboard side of the hull was protected from shipworm and gribble by the ‘blanket’ of organic rich silts of the seabed which cut off the oxygen
hwreck-01-c3.claim: The starboard side lay buried under a blanket of organic-rich silt that cut off the oxygen, so shipworm and gribble could not live there.

hwreck-02-c1.text: Mary Zapheiropoulou (2012). The Antikythera shipwreck and the treasures. From Antikythera to the Square Kilometre Array: Lessons from the Ancients (Proceedings of Science).
hwreck-02-c1.quote: However, at a depth of about 50 meters and at a distance of 25 meters from the coast, he located a very important ancient shipwreck.
hwreck-02-c1.claim: At a depth of about 50 metres, some 25 metres from the shore, he found an ancient wreck instead, and he came back up holding the arm of a bronze statue.

hwreck-02-c2.text: Mary Zapheiropoulou (2012). The Antikythera shipwreck and the treasures. From Antikythera to the Square Kilometre Array: Lessons from the Ancients (Proceedings of Science).
hwreck-02-c2.quote: By then one of the divers had died and two permanently disabled by their work.
hwreck-02-c2.claim: The operation lasted ten months, until the end of September 1901, and by then one diver had died and two had been permanently disabled.

hwreck-02-c3.text: Jo Marchant (2016). Human Skeleton Found on Famed Antikythera Shipwreck. Scientific American (reprinted from Nature).
hwreck-02-c3.quote: But on August 31 this year, investigators made another groundbreaking discovery: a human skeleton, buried under around half a metre of pottery sherds and sand.
hwreck-02-c3.claim: On 31 August 2016 the divers uncovered a human skeleton under about half a metre of pottery sherds and sand

hwreck-03-c1.text: Institute of Nautical Archaeology (2015). Key Figures. Institute of Nautical Archaeology.
hwreck-03-c1.quote: After taking only six diving lessons at a local YMCA, he left for Turkey where he directed the excavation of the wreck about a hundred feet deep off Cape Gelidonya.
hwreck-03-c1.claim: He took only six diving lessons at a local YMCA before leaving for Turkey.

hwreck-03-c1.text: Institute of Nautical Archaeology (2020). Cape Gelidonya Late Bronze Age Shipwreck Excavation. Institute of Nautical Archaeology.
hwreck-03-c1.quote: In 1960, it was the first shipwreck excavation carried out to completion on the sea bed, the first conducted according to the standards of terrestrial excavation, and the first directed by a diving archaeologist.
hwreck-03-c1.claim: In 1960 Gelidonya became the first shipwreck excavation carried out to completion on the seabed, the first conducted to the standards of an excavation on land, and the first directed by an archaeologist who dived himself.

hwreck-03-c2.text: Institute of Nautical Archaeology (2020). Cape Gelidonya Late Bronze Age Shipwreck Excavation. Institute of Nautical Archaeology.
hwreck-03-c2.quote: The conclusion was that the ship was probably Canaanite, or early Phoenician although there was the possibility that the ship was Cypriot, because so many Near Eastern artifacts were found on Cyprus from the same period.
hwreck-03-c2.claim: The excavators concluded that the ship was probably Canaanite or early Phoenician, though it might have been Cypriot, because so many Near Eastern objects turn up on Cyprus in this period.

hwreck-03-c3.text: Mary Rose Trust (2024). Raising the Mary Rose. Mary Rose Trust.
hwreck-03-c3.quote: A grid of bright yellow pipe was erected over the site, essentially dividing it up into small areas corresponding with the decks and main beams of the ship.
hwreck-03-c3.claim: A grid of bright yellow pipe divided the site into small areas matching the ship's decks and main beams, and every artefact and timber was recorded on a uniquely numbered dive log.

hwreck-04-c1.text: Institute of Nautical Archaeology (2020). Uluburun Late Bronze Age Shipwreck Excavation. Institute of Nautical Archaeology.
hwreck-04-c1.quote: The Uluburun shipwreck was excavated by INA over 11 seasons between 1984 and 1994, with more than 22,000 dives logged to depths in excess of 150 feet.
hwreck-04-c1.claim: The Institute of Nautical Archaeology excavated it over 11 seasons between 1984 and 1994, logging more than 22,000 dives and raising about 17 tonnes of artefacts.

hwreck-04-c2.text: Institute of Nautical Archaeology (2020). Uluburun Late Bronze Age Shipwreck Excavation. Institute of Nautical Archaeology.
hwreck-04-c2.quote: The Uluburun ship was transporting a bulk cargo of copper and tin ingots, in the usual ratio of 10:1 to produce bronze.
hwreck-04-c2.claim: The Uluburun ship was carrying copper and tin in the usual ratio of 10:1 for making bronze.

hwreck-04-c3.text: Sara Savat (2022). Findings from 3,000-year-old Uluburun shipwreck reveal complex trade network. The Source, Washington University in St. Louis.
hwreck-04-c3.quote: One-third of the tin aboard the Uluburun shipwreck was sourced from the Mušiston mine in Uzbekistan.
hwreck-04-c3.claim: About one-third of the tin, they concluded, came from the Mušiston mine in Central Asia, more than 2,000 miles from Haifa, and two-thirds from Kestel.

hwreck-04-c3.text: Daniel Berger, Kai Kaniuth, Gerhard Brügmann, Ernst Pernicka (2023). Why Central Asia’s Mushiston is not a source for the Late Bronze Age tin ingots from the Uluburun shipwreck. Frontiers in Earth Science.
hwreck-04-c3.quote: This means that there is never an unambiguous answer to the question of tin provenance using tin isotopes alone.
hwreck-04-c3.claim: Tin isotope values vary widely within a deposit and overlap heavily between deposits, so tin isotopes alone never give an unambiguous answer.

hwreck-05-c1.text: Vasa Museum. Timeline. Vasa Museum (Swedish National Maritime and Transport Museums).
hwreck-05-c1.quote: He has thirty men run back and forth across the deck and the ship rolls alarmingly.
hwreck-05-c1.claim: He had thirty men run back and forth across the deck, and the ship rolled so alarmingly that Fleming stopped the test for fear she would sink at the quay.

hwreck-05-c2.text: Mary Rose Trust (2024). Why did the Mary Rose sink?. Mary Rose Trust.
hwreck-05-c2.quote: She was 34 years old when she sank, and had travelled hundreds of miles, from Scotland in the north to the Atlantic coast of France in the south, during her career.
hwreck-05-c2.claim: Henry VIII's warship was built in Portsmouth from 1510 and served for 34 years, sailing as far as Scotland in the north and the Atlantic coast of France in the south.

hwreck-05-c3.text: Vasa Museum. The conservation of Vasa. Vasa Museum (Swedish National Maritime and Transport Museums).
hwreck-05-c3.quote: The spray treatment lasted 17 years, from April 1962 to January 1979, followed by another 9 years of slow air-drying.
hwreck-05-c3.claim: The spray treatment lasted 17 years, from April 1962 to January 1979, and was followed by nine years of slow air-drying.

hwreck-06-c1.text: University of Southampton (2018). Black Sea expedition discovers world's oldest intact shipwreck. University of Southampton News.
hwreck-06-c1.quote: A small piece of the vessel was carbon dated, confirming the ship to be at least 2,400 years old.
hwreck-06-c1.claim: A small piece of the vessel was carbon dated, confirming that the ship is at least 2,400 years old, from around 400 BCE.

hwreck-06-c2.text: Jonathan Amos (2022). Endurance: Shackleton's lost ship is found in Antarctic. BBC News.
hwreck-06-c2.quote: Endurance was spotted in the Weddell Sea at a depth of 3,008m.
hwreck-06-c2.claim: Endurance was spotted in the Weddell Sea at a depth of 3,008 metres, about four miles south of Worsley's estimated position, on the 100th anniversary of Shackleton's funeral.

hwreck-06-c3.text: Brandon Specktor (2019). The Titanic Shipwreck Is Collapsing into Rust, First Visit in 14 Years Reveals. Live Science.
hwreck-06-c3.quote: Henrietta Mann, one of the researchers who described the bacteria, predicted that the microbes could devour the entire Titanic shipwreck by 2030.
hwreck-06-c3.claim: Henrietta Mann, one of the scientists who described the bacterium, predicted that the microbes could devour the entire wreck by 2030, yet the bow and many interiors were still well preserved in 2019.

hwreck-07-c1.text: United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit (Black, Circuit Judge) (2011). Odyssey Marine Exploration, Inc. v. Unidentified Shipwrecked Vessel (Kingdom of Spain, claimant). United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.
hwreck-07-c1.quote: Odyssey ultimately recovered approximately 594,000 coins and a number of other small artifacts.
hwreck-07-c1.claim: Odyssey recovered approximately 594,000 coins and a number of other small artefacts

hwreck-07-c2.text: UNESCO (2001). Convention on the Protection of the Underwater Cultural Heritage. UNESCO Legal Affairs.
hwreck-07-c2.quote: The preservation in situ of underwater cultural heritage shall be considered as the first option before allowing or engaging in any activities directed at this heritage.
hwreck-07-c2.claim: preservation where the heritage lies is to be considered as the first option before any activity directed at it.

hwreck-07-c3.text: Peace Palace Library (2016). Java Sea: Dutch, British and U.S. WW II Shipwrecks destroyed by Illegal Scavenging. Peace Palace Library blog.
hwreck-07-c3.quote: In the United Kingdom, only 67 ship wrecks and all underwater military aircraft are "protected places" under the Protection of Military Remains Act 1986 which imposes restrictions on their exploration and marine salvage.
hwreck-07-c3.claim: In the United Kingdom only 67 ship wrecks, plus all military aircraft lost under water, are protected places under the Protection of Military Remains Act 1986
